newsitem.title: UK: UK's Heseltine sees stark danger of Tory disunity.
newsitem.headline: UK's Heseltine sees stark danger of Tory disunity.

text.p: UK Deputy Prime Minister Michael Heseltine warned members of the ruling Conservative party to close ranks or open the door to a Labour victory at Britain's forthcoming general election.
"The danger of disunity in the Conservative party is a stark one, which has one consequence -- a Labour threat..." Heseltine told BBC radio on Monday.

"What would be a disaster would be to allow Labour to get back into power with all the threats to our living standards and our tax levels that that would mean because of apparent disunity in the Conservative party," he added.
Conservative unity is likely to be tested later this month when "Euro-sceptic" member of parliament Teresa Gorman introduces a bill calling for a referendum on Britain's role in Europe.
Heseltine curtly dismissed Gorman's proposal, saying it was not something that was on the mind of most British voters.
Asked what he was going to do about her, he answered: "I'm not going to do anything about Teresa Gorman."
Earlier, Gorman said 80-90 percent of her constituents shared her sceptical view on Europe.
She told BBC radio that passing a bill that called for a plebiscite would counter the threat to the Conservative party posed by Sir James Goldsmith's Referendum party.
"We want to stop that by backing a bill for a proper referendum which would ask people whether they want us to renegotiate for a free trade deal and nothing more," Gorman said.
